description: Global coordination supports climate investment development finance and just transition.
Output expands but gains concentrate and social legitimacy weakens.
Trade conflict debt pressure and weak coordination reduce development capacity.
Climate impacts and adaptation costs reshape development choices.
High debt service and expensive capital crowd out public investment.
Technology diffuses unevenly and productivity gaps widen.
Health education care and social protection anchor broad-based development.
Food energy and commodity volatility destabilize development planning.
